root_cause_hypothesis: The post-take inspection sequence blindly runs every candidate verb (examine, read, look inside) on an object without checking whether a prior verb already returned identical output, so redundant verbs are executed and wasted.
change_summary: In process_agent_step, when an inspection verb outcome is recorded, capture a normalized hash/signature of the response text on the entity's verb_outcomes so identical responses can be detected. In determine_next_action, when building the inspection sequence for a taken object and when advancing step_index, skip any remaining verb whose expected response would duplicate one already seen for that object (i.e. once a verb returns a response matching a previously-recorded response signature for the same target, prune the rest of the sequence). This uses only deterministic string comparison of already-captured responses — no new LLM calls on the hot path.
acceptance_criteria: In a future run log, after taking an object like 'golden ball', at most one of {examine, read, look inside} that produces a given response text is executed; subsequent verbs yielding an identical response are not emitted as actions.

The game_log entries for the object's inspection verbs show distinct 'response' values, or the inspection sequence terminates early (inspection['target'] cleared) once a duplicate response signature is detected.
The step range that previously showed 3 identical successive responses (steps 41-44) shrinks to a single informative step plus at most one distinct follow-up when replayed on the same scenario.
known_entities[target]['verb_outcomes'] records enough signal (e.g. a response signature) to demonstrate duplicate detection was the reason for pruning.
risk_notes: Must not persist response signatures or 'blocked' outcomes to strategy JSON, since responses are state-dependent; keep signatures in-memory on the run state only. Response normalization must ignore volatile substrings (timestamps, score lines) to avoid false-negatives. Pruning too aggressively could skip a verb that legitimately reveals new info in a different game state, so only prune within the same object's current inspection pass, not permanently.
deferred_reason: Identical response to examine does not prove drop/throw/wear would also be redundant. Re-evaluate if a future run shows this causing meaningful progress loss.
